title: HCMC Marathon 2027 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: HCMC Marathon Review: Course, Cool January Air, Cut-offs
meta_description: HCMC Marathon review: the January 2026 race from 30/4 Park, 21°C at the 3am start, a course open until 9.30am, partly open roads, 1,829 marathon finishers and field depth.
dek: What it was like to run Ho Chi Minh City's January marathon in 2026: a start beside the Independence Palace, a course under and over the Saigon River, air that was cool for Saigon, cut-offs, partly open roads and how fast the field ran.
verdict: Enter if you want a January city marathon in Vietnam that starts and finishes beside the Independence Palace and runs in air that is cool for Saigon. At the 3am start in 2026 it was 21°C with a dew point of 19°C, and still only 26°C when the course closed at 9.30am. Nearly 11,000 runners from 75 countries took part, and 1,829 finished the marathon, with a median of 4:29. The catch is the roads and the clock. Roads are only partly closed and the organiser warns of traffic lights, and the 2027 marathon limit is a strict six hours, half an hour shorter than the course stayed open in 2026. Train for six hours, not six and a half.

sections.heading: The Course: From the Independence Palace, Under and Over the Saigon River
paragraphs: All three races start and finish at 30/4 Park on Le Duan Street, in front of the Independence Palace [1][2]. The organiser calls it the only race that starts and finishes in the heart of Saigon [2]. In 2026 the route passed City Hall, the Nguyen Hue walking street, Ben Thanh market, the Bitexco tower, Notre-Dame Cathedral and the Ba Son Bridge [1], and ran through six wards: Saigon, An Khanh, Cat Lai, Thao Dien, Thanh My Tay and Binh Trung [3].

The marathon map on the official site shows a loop through the old centre on Ton Duc Thang, Dong Khoi and Nguyen Hue; an out-and-back along Vo Van Kiet to a U-turn at Nguyen Van Cu; the Thu Thiem tunnel under the Saigon River; a long leg east along Mai Chi Tho and Tran Quy Kien, past Diamond Island, to a U-turn on Nguyen Van Kinh; and crossings of the Thu Thiem Bridge and the Ba Son Bridge [4]. The 2026 police road notice names the same riverside section of Vo Van Kiet, from Nguyen Van Cu to the tunnel [5]. Timing mats in 2026 were at 7.4 km, 10 km, 12.8 km, 27.5 km, 35.5 km and 39.6 km [6].

sections.heading: The Weather: Cool for Saigon
paragraphs: Tan Son Nhat airport, about 6.5 km north-west of the start, recorded 21°C at 3am on race morning, with a dew point of 19°C, 88% humidity and no wind [7]. It stayed at 21°C to 22°C, with a dew point of 18°C to 19°C, until 7.30am, with mist from 6am. It then warmed to 23°C at 8am, 25°C at 9am and 26°C, with 61% humidity, at 9.30am, when the marathon course closed [7].

A dew point of 18°C to 19°C is humid but manageable, well below the mid-20s that make tropical racing punishing. The men's winner, Huynh Anh Khoi, credited the cool weather and a favourable course for a best-ever result in the city [8]. Runners still out after 8am finished in 23°C to 26°C air [7].

sections.heading: Time Limits, Aid and Finisher Items
paragraphs: The 2026 rules set a maximum finish time of six hours from the marathon start, with the course reopening to traffic on a rolling schedule and the aid stations closing with the streets [9]. In practice the police notice kept the marathon course closed until 9.30am, six and a half hours after the 3am start; the half marathon ran from 3.30am to 7am and the 10 km from 4.15am to 6.15am [5]. The results list 118 official marathon finishers slower than six hours, the slowest in 6:30:42 [6].

The route map on the official site gives closing times for six marathon checkpoints: 4.10am at the Vo Van Kiet U-turn, 5.25am on To Huu, 7.15am at the Nguyen Van Kinh U-turn, 8.05am on Tran Quy Kien, 8.30am on Bui Thien Ngo and 9.10am near the Ba Son Bridge [4]. The organiser says runners are not allowed to continue past a checkpoint after its cut-off, and that water and medical stations close once traffic is back [10].

The race listing for 2026 describes refreshment stations every 2 km with water, electrolyte drinks and fruit [11]. Finishers inside the limit get a medal, and marathon finishers a finisher shirt [9]. The results also list 36 marathon entrants as disqualified, 33 of them with a finish time [6]; the rules say runners with missing or irregular split times are reviewed for disqualification [9].

sections.heading: The Roads: Partly Open, With Traffic Lights
paragraphs: Only part of each road is closed. The 2026 police notice kept vehicles off the race lanes along the route but let traffic use the rest of the road; two-wheelers were barred from the riverside lane of Vo Van Kiet from 3am to 9.30am, and the stretch of Le Duan beside the start was closed to all vehicles from 9 to 12 January [5]. The organiser warns that because the race runs through the city centre, runners may be held up by traffic lights, and asks them to follow the event staff's instructions [10]. The early start is there partly to reduce traffic pressure in the centre [2].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: Huynh Anh Khoi won the marathon in 2:25:44, Khoi's first marathon win at the race after three straight years of taking part, ahead of Cambodia's Vann Pheara in 2:27:24 and Le Van Tuan in 2:34:18 [12][8]. Pham Thi Hong Le won the women's race in 2:46:18, from Le Thi Ha (2:57:28) and Nguyen Thi Ngoc Lan (2:58:39) [12][8].

The field thins fast behind them. Tenth place was 2:46:37 for men and 3:31:30 for women, and only 36 runners broke three hours. Of 1,829 official finishers, 171 ran under 3:30 and 572 under four hours, and the median was 4:29:01 [6]. The marathon is mostly Vietnamese: 1,476 finishers were listed as Vietnamese, followed by Japan (53), China (49) and South Korea (42) [6].

The half marathon was won by Hoang Nguyen Thanh in 1:08:31 and Hoang Thi Ngoc Hoa in 1:20:56 [8]. Tenth place was 1:19:26 for men and 1:37:11 for women, and the median of 3,410 finishers was 2:26:14 [6]. The SEA Games gold medallist Nguyen Trung Cuong won the 10 km on a first appearance at the race [8], in 31:18 [6].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: The race opened on Friday 9 January at the Hoa Lu Sports Centre, and bibs and race kits were collected on 9 and 10 January [1][11]. A marathon village of nearly 40 booths ran alongside [3].

For 2027 the organiser lists bib collection at the Hoa Lu Sports Center, 2 Dinh Tien Hoang Street, on Friday 15 and Saturday 16 January, and none on race morning; you need your passport or ID [10]. The 2027 kit is a singlet, bib with chip, finisher medal, finisher T-shirt, e-certificate, post-race food and bag drop [10]. Fees are not refundable; a transfer costs VND 300,000 and a change of distance VND 100,000 [10]. Marathon fees for non-residents run from VND 1,250,000 to VND 2,450,000 (about US$48 to US$93) depending on when you enter, and from VND 810,000 to VND 1,925,000 for residents [13].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a big January marathon in Vietnam with a central start and finish, air that was 21°C to 22°C for most of the 2026 race, and a field where a sub-3:30 marathon puts you in roughly the top 170.

Think twice if you need fully closed roads, or if you need more than six hours: in 2026, 118 finishers took longer, and the organiser's 2027 rules say no one may continue past a checkpoint after its cut-off.

The 2027 race is on Sunday 17 January, from 30/4 Park, with the marathon starting at 3am and a six-hour limit (9am); the half marathon has three and a half hours and the 10 km two [10][14][15]. It is a different race from the Techcombank Ho Chi Minh City International Marathon, which Sunrise Events Vietnam holds in December, next on 6 December 2026 [16]; the HCMC Marathon is run by Pulse Active [15].

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's race information and route map, the 2026 rules, the full results, the police road notice, airport weather records and Vietnamese press reports.

faqs.question: What time does the HCMC Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Very early. In 2026 the marathon started at 3am, the half marathon at 3.30am and the 10 km at 4.15am, all from 30/4 Park on Le Duan Street. The organiser says the early start eases traffic in the city centre. For 2027 the marathon again starts at 3am, on Sunday 17 January.

faqs.question: How hot is the HCMC Marathon in January?
faqs.answer: Cool for Saigon. At the 3am start in 2026, Tan Son Nhat airport recorded 21°C, a dew point of 19°C and 88% humidity, and it stayed at 21°C to 22°C until 7.30am. It reached 26°C with 61% humidity by 9.30am, when the marathon course closed. The men's winner credited the cool weather.

faqs.question: What is the cut-off time for the HCMC Marathon?
faqs.answer: Six hours for the marathon in 2027, so 9am, with three and a half hours for the half and two for the 10 km. The 2026 rules also said six hours, but the course stayed open until 9.30am and 118 runners finished slower. In 2027 runners may not continue past a checkpoint after its cut-off.

faqs.question: Are the roads closed for the HCMC Marathon?
faqs.answer: Only partly. In 2026 the police kept vehicles off the race lanes but let traffic use the rest of each road, and barred two-wheelers from the Vo Van Kiet riverside lane until 9.30am. The organiser warns that runners may be stopped by traffic lights and should follow the event staff.

faqs.question: Is the HCMC Marathon the same race as the Techcombank Ho Chi Minh City International Marathon?
faqs.answer: No. The HCMC Marathon is held in January by Pulse Active, from 30/4 Park, and its 2027 race is on 17 January. The Techcombank Ho Chi Minh City International Marathon is a separate race organised by Sunrise Events Vietnam, held in December; its next edition is on 6 December 2026.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-29 about the previous edition (11 January 2026). This is the January HCMC Marathon, not the December Techcombank race. Weather is from Tan Son Nhat airport METAR observations, not a forecast. Field-depth figures come from the full official Sportstats results, counting only finishers without a status. The 2026 rules set a six-hour limit, but the police notice kept the course open until 9.30am and the results include finishers up to 6:30:42; both are given. The posted route map is not clearly dated, so it is described as the map on the official site. No first-hand runner account of the 2026 race was found. No rating.
